title: Drinfeld Doubles and Yetter–Drinfeld Module Constructions

items.title: Left-left Yetter–Drinfeld module
items.statement: A left-left Yetter–Drinfeld H-module is a vector space V with a unital left H-action and a counital coassociative left H-coaction δ(v)=Σv−1⊗v0 satisfying δ(hv)=Σh1v−1S(h3)⊗h2v0. Maps preserve both structures. For f∈H*, set f·v=Σf(v−1)v0; with f⊙g=g*f this is a left H*op action.
items.strategy: State both structures and the compatibility equation explicitly, then verify the dual action from coassociativity and counitality. No finite-dimensionality is needed for this definition or its action check.

references.title: G. A. García and C. Vay, Simple modules of small quantum groups at dihedral groups, Doc. Math. 29 (2024), §3.1.3
Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych and Victor Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §7.15

items.title: Finite Drinfeld double: convention and candidate multiplication
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra H over a field k with bijective antipode S, set D(H)=H*op⊗H in normal order f h. Give H* its dual coproduct Δf(x,y)=f(xy), ordinary convolution * on H*, and opposite product f⊙g=g*f. Define χ(h⊗f)=Σf1(S(h1))f3(h3)f2⊗h2 and (f⊗h)(g⊗k)=Σg1(S(h1))g3(h3)(g2*f)⊗h2k, with unit ε⊗1. This is a candidate product; associativity is proved separately.
items.strategy: Fix and type-check the finite dual and H*op convention before using it. The HH-8 bijective-antipode supplier is required for the stated unconditional application; this record does not independently verify that supplier.

references.title: Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations, lecture notes, §4.3
Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych and Victor Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §7.14
G. A. García and C. Vay, Simple modules of small quantum groups at dihedral groups, Doc. Math. 29 (2024), §3.1.3

items.title: Double crossing laws and associativity
items.statement: For the candidate product of def-hh-finite-double-cross-relations, χ is a unital distributive law in both inputs, the product is associative and unital, and the two canonical maps H*op→D(H) and H→D(H) are injective algebra maps.
items.strategy: Pair χ with x∈H, verify the two multiplication laws on both sides using the dual coproduct and ΔS, then use those exact map identities to compare the two associations of three simple tensors. The normal tensor product gives injective embeddings.

references.title: Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations, lecture notes, §4.3

items.title: Double coalgebra, multiplicativity, and antipode
items.statement: On the associative algebra D(H), set ΔD(fh)=Σ(f1h1)⊗(f2h2) and εD(fh)=f(1)ε(h). Then ΔD and εD are algebra maps and ΔD is coassociative; S_D(fh)=S(h)(f∘S−1) is an antipode. Thus these maps give D(H) a Hopf algebra structure.
items.strategy: Tensor coalgebra axioms give coassociativity and counits. Pair the cross relation against x,y to check Δ multiplicativity and against 1 for ε multiplicativity. Define the reversing antipode, verify it preserves the crossing, then compute both antipode contractions.

references.title: Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations, lecture notes, §4.3
Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych and Victor Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §7.14

items.title: Modules over the finite double are left-left Yetter–Drinfeld modules
items.statement: For finite-dimensional H with bijective antipode, restriction and coaction reconstruction give inverse equivalences between left D(H)-modules and left-left Yetter–Drinfeld H-modules. The equivalence preserves tensor products, and the Yetter–Drinfeld category is braided by c(v⊗w)=Σv−1·w⊗v0, with inverse c−1(w⊗v)=Σv0⊗S−1(v−1)·w.
items.strategy: Recover the coaction from the H*op action by finite duality and prove its axioms by pairing with dual functionals. The inverse crossing is obtained from χ by antipode cancellation; it is exactly the Yetter–Drinfeld equation. Check inverse functors, tensor product coaction, braiding, inverse, linearity and hexagons explicitly.

references.title: G. A. García and C. Vay, Simple modules of small quantum groups at dihedral groups, Doc. Math. 29 (2024), §3.1.3

Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations, lecture notes, §4.3

items.title: Finite double and its canonical quasitriangular structure
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra H with bijective antipode, the tensor R=Σi(fi⊗1)⊗(ε⊗hi), for any dual bases (hi),(fi), is basis-independent and invertible with inverse Σi(fi⊗1)⊗(ε⊗S−1(hi)). It satisfies RΔD(d)=ΔDop(d)R, (ΔD⊗id)R=R13R23, and (id⊗ΔD)R=R13R12. On every left D(H)-module pair, τR is the Yetter–Drinfeld braiding.
items.strategy: Use finite duality to identify the canonical tensor with the identity, evaluate both products with the proposed inverse against the dual basis, identify τR with the Yetter–Drinfeld braiding, and recover each quasitriangular identity by applying the proved module identities to regular D(H) modules and evaluating at the tensor unit.

title: Drinfeld Doubles and Yetter–Drinfeld Module Constructions — Examples

items.title: The full dual of an infinite group algebra has no transpose coproduct
items.statement: If G is infinite and H=kG, the transpose of multiplication on H sends the functional δe∈H* to the function (a,b)↦δe(ab), which is not an element of H*⊗H*. Thus the full linear dual cannot carry the coalgebra coproduct transposed from multiplication in the algebraic tensor category.
items.strategy: A finite tensor sum gives a finite-dimensional span of row functions. The rows of (a,b)↦δe(ab) are infinitely many distinct point masses, which are linearly independent.

references.title: Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations, lecture notes, §4.3 and §4.4
Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych and Victor Ostrik, Tensor Categories, §7.14

items.title: The Drinfeld double of a finite group algebra
items.statement: For a finite group G over a field k, the finite double D(kG) has basis δx⊗g and multiplication (δx⊗g)(δy⊗h)=1[x=gyg−1]δx⊗gh, coproduct Σab=x(δa⊗g)⊗(δb⊗g), and canonical R=Σx(δx⊗e)⊗(ε⊗x). Left-left Yetter–Drinfeld modules are G-graded spaces with conjugation-compatible action and braiding c(vx⊗w)=x·w⊗vx.
items.strategy: Insert group-like coproducts and the point-mass dual basis into the finite-double formulas; verify the resulting structure maps, R, and braided-module formula directly.

references.title: Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations, lecture notes, Example 4.21 and Exercise 42
G. A. García and C. Vay, Simple modules of small quantum groups at dihedral groups, Doc. Math. 29 (2024), §3.1.3

items.title: A nonabelian group makes the double cross-relations noncommutative
items.statement: In D(kS3), for p=(12), q=(23), and r=(13)=pqp, the elements (δr⊗p) and (δq⊗e) do not commute, and the conjugation-graded module kS3 has a braiding that differs from the ordinary flip.
items.strategy: Use the finite-group multiplication and braiding formulas and compute the two products and one basis-tensor image explicitly.

references.title: Kalle Kytölä, Introduction to Hopf algebras and representations, lecture notes, Exercise 42
